Aerial Wildlife 
Survey Report 
WMU 360 Aerial Ungulate Survey (January 2018) 
 
Background 
Wildlife Management Unit (WMU) 360 covers an area of 4,757.20 km 2 and is located immediately south of the 
town of High Prairie. The WMU is bounded to the south by WMU 351, and extends east to Highway 33, then west 
to Highway 49 and finally Highway 2 to the north.  Within its boarders are Snipe Lake (42.11 km 2) and East Prairie 
Metis Settlement (334.44 km2). 
 
The most recent moose (Alces alces) survey in WMU 360 was completed during the winter of 2013-14 using the 
Distance Sampling method. The estimated population density was 0.65 moose/ km 2 and the estimated population 
size was 2,754 moose (90% CI 2155 – 3519). The age-sex composition ratio (bull:calf:100cow) based on the 
moose observed was 28:42:100.  
 
The objective of this distance survey was to estimated total population size, population densities, and age -sex 
composition ratios of moose in WMU 360 to inform game management decisions.  
  
Methods 
An aerial ungulate survey was conducted in WMU 360 during January 23, 24, and 26 using the distance sampling 
method (Buckland et al. 2001). A total of 62 parallel east-west transects lines (survey effort 542.10 km, interval 
1.2 km) were flown with a Bell 206 Jet Ranger over 3 days, with 1 weather day on the 25 th). Data were analyzed 
using the program “Distance” (Version 6.0, Release 2; Thomas et al. 2010).  
  
Results 
A total of 180 moose were observed in 112 groups. Of these 32 (17.8%) were bulls, 90 (50.0%) were cows and 
58 (32.2%) were calves which yielded an age-sex composition ratio (bull:calf:100cow) of 36:64:100. The 
encounter rate was 0.21 moose/km and the mean group (cluster) size was 1.61. The final estimated moose 
density in WMU 360 was 0.50 moose/km2 (90% CI 0.386 – 0.650), and the estimated abundance was 2,382 
moose (90% CI 1834 – 3094; Table 1). These results include observations made within the East Prairie Metis 
Settlement.
